3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: Serge took a left turn and drove through the tiny streets of Jen. The city looked surprisingly clean and well-maintained. There was no sign of the destruction the city suffered during one of the heaviest battles of the Civil War.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: Today was a day of special symbolic importance for Sordland. Every year, on the 14th of March, proud patriots from all ages gathered to celebrate the end of the Sordish Civil War and Tarquin Soll's victory.

6.speaker: Narrator
6.text: Serge drove us to the city of Jen, the stronghold of Sordish nationalists, for an event organized by the opposition parties to discuss current events. In reality, it was probably a publicity stunt, to show Sordland that the leaders of the Assembly could sit around the same table.
6.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Autocrat_Path"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.BergiaSpecialZone_Proposal_Amendment"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.BergiaSpecialZone_Proposal_Amendment"] == true) == false)

7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: The National Front Party, which governed the city, undoubtedly had the biggest hand in the organization of the meeting. It was not a coincidence that it fell on "Victory Day".

8.speaker: Narrator
8.text: Jen had survived one of the worst atrocities of the war, and its Victory Day celebrations were the most jubilant in all of Sordland.

9.speaker: Petr Vectern
9.text: "Wow. That was too comfortable of a drive to have been this fast."

10.speaker: Serge Wolkner
10.text: "Mr. President. Mr. Vice President. We are about to arrive at the Jen Center of Culture. Ms. Morgna had already arrived and she will be waiting for you."

11.speaker: Narrator
11.text: Petr was sitting next to me in the presidential car, skimming through the morning newspaper in silence. Suddenly, Serge rolled down the soundproof window.

12.speaker: Narrator
12.text: Petr raised his head to look out the window. He folded the newspaper and laid it beside him.

13.speaker: Serge Wolkner
13.text: "I hope the journey was comfortable, sir."

15.speaker: Player
15.text: "See? I wasn't joking. Serge is the best."

16.speaker: Serge Wolkner
16.text: "We have a yard now, and the children have more room to play."

17.speaker: Serge Wolkner
17.text: "It makes me proud to be driving the two most important men in Sordland on Victory Day."

18.speaker: Serge Wolkner
18.text: "You are embarrassing me, sir. I'm no special man. It's the Kadilla."

19.speaker: Petr Vectern
19.text: "Nah, I should ride with you guys more often. I can't believe I could actually read on the go."

20.speaker: Petr Vectern
20.text: "Although I sure wouldn't mind navigating her dangerous curves one day."

22.speaker: Petr Vectern
22.text: "No kidding. My driver Sveta can't hold a candle to him."

24.speaker: Petr Vectern
24.text: "The three most important men are right here in this car, Serge."

25.speaker: Petr Vectern
25.text: "Looks like the NFP mayors have really transformed the city. Wasn't this an abandoned warehouse for the longest time?"

26.speaker: Serge Wolkner
26.text: "I believe it used to function as a rebel militia base during -- and a little while after -- the Civil War."

29.speaker: Player
29.text: "It's been a while since I've heard that name."

30.speaker: Player
30.text: "Let's not sour the mood with memories of the Civil War."

32.speaker: Petr Vectern
32.text: "Sorry to bring it up. May it never be spoken again."

33.speaker: Petr Vectern
33.text: "If you remember, they used places like this to organize in the '30s. Luckily for us, Soll handled them long ago."

34.speaker: Narrator
34.text: Serge stopped the car and went outside to hold our doors.

35.speaker: Serge Wolkner
35.text: "Here we are, sirs. I hope you have a great day."

36.speaker: Narrator
36.text: We got out of the car and walked towards the entrance of the building. Every spot around us was decorated with the flags of Sordland.

37.speaker: Narrator
37.text: We slowed down in front of a colorful plaza overlooking a massive concrete building with a giant sign that read: "Jen Center of Culture."

38.speaker: Petr Vectern
38.text: "Well... Maybe not all of them. Their *democratic* counterparts like the Young Sords lived on, after all..."

46.speaker: Narrator
46.text: Serge drove us to the city of Jen, the Sordish nationalist stronghold, for an event organized to celebrate Victory Day and commemorate the fallen of the Battle of Jen.
46.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Autocrat_Path"] == true) and (Variable["BaseGame.BergiaSpecialZone_Proposal_Amendment"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.BergiaSpecialZone_Proposal_Amendment"] == true) == false)

47.speaker: Narrator
47.text: For the National Front Party, which governed the city, the day undoubtedly had great meaning. A lot of their supporters could be seen outside waving party flags.

48.speaker: Narrator
48.text: But today had great symbolic importance for Sordland as a whole too. Every year, on the 14th of March, proud patriots from all ages gathered to celebrate the end of the Sordish Civil War and Tarquin Soll's victory.

49.speaker: Narrator
49.text: Jen had survived one of the worst atrocities of the war, and its Victory Day celebrations were the most jubilant in all of Sordland. Petr and I both decided to attend.

53.speaker: Narrator
53.text: Originally, only Petr and I were scheduled to attend. But after learning about new developments with the Ishval Ersen case, Nia Morgna was invited as well. Representatives from both the PFJP and NFP had told us they wanted to talk about the case in more detail.

54.speaker: Narrator
54.text: Nia departed Holsord first. Petr and I left on our own a little later.

58.speaker: Narrator
58.text: For the National Front Party, which governed the city, the day undoubtedly had great meaning. Due to the significance of the day and the NFP's lobbying efforts, the celebrations were allowed to take place despite the emergency.

59.speaker: Narrator
59.text: After bidding our farewells, Kesaro took us outside the building to join the Victory Day event on the plaza.

60.speaker: Narrator
60.text: Together, we walked up to the center of the plaza.

64.speaker: Serge Wolkner
64.text: "Mr. President. Mr. Vice President. We are about to arrive at the Jen Center of Culture. We are slightly earlier than estimated."

245.speaker: Serge Wolkner
245.text: "I'm good, sir. In fact, Suzan and I moved to a new house recently."

246.speaker: Petr Vectern
246.text: "Amazing, Serge. Anton must be treating you *very* well."

251.speaker: Serge Wolkner
251.text: "I'm just fine, sir. Thanks for asking."
